thread:
Alex Kim: Quick FYI — I'm pushing a small change to reduce noisy alerts from the nightly batch workers. Saw ~40% of pages last night were the batch timeout rule firing during the big ETL sweep.
Maya Patel: Thanks for the heads-up. What exactly are you changing?
Alex Kim: Lowering sensitivity for the batch-job latency rule and routing those alerts to #eng-batch instead of #eng-oncall during the 02:00-04:30 window.
Alex Kim: Config snippet I'm applying (will roll as a knob boolean first):
```yaml
alert: BatchJobHighLatency
expr: job:batch_latency_seconds:95th > 60
for: 10m
severity: page
routes:
  - channel: eng-batch
    active_hours: 02:00-04:30
  - channel: eng-oncall
    fallback: true
```
Jordan Lee: Routing to eng-batch sounds good. Can we keep a short window where it still pages eng-oncall if it spikes super-high?
Alex Kim: Yep — fallback is still true, and I'll add an override for >120s to always page.
Sam Rivera: Will this affect the dedupe keys? We had duplicated pages for the same job before.
Alex Kim: No change to dedupe key, just threshold + routing. Should reduce duplicates overall since fewer low-severity pages will go to the core oncall.
Linh Tran: Can you ping me when it's live? I'll watch for regressions during the 02:00 run.
Alex Kim: Will do. Rolling to canary now for our dev cluster (5% traffic) — will monitor for 15m then promote.
oncall-bot: alerting-config-bot: Config change submitted by Alex Kim to staging: batch-latency-routing v2. ID: cfg_20260317_77
Maya Patel: Thanks — please add a short note to the oncall handoff doc so night shifters know the routing change.
Alex Kim: Added note to the handoff doc and linked in #eng-oncall: https://redwood.internal/docs/oncall/handoffs/nightly-batches
Jordan Lee: :thumbsup: If you see any unexpected missing pages, revert the routing boolean.
Alex Kim: Agreed. If anything odd happens I'll flip back and leave a note in the thread.
Sam Rivera: Thanks — I'll check PagerDuty escalation mapping after you promote.
Alex Kim: Promotion done to prod canary at 1767111312. Monitoring.
Linh Tran: Saw one spike at 1767111378 but it stayed under the override threshold. No pages routed to oncall.
Alex Kim: Good. Promoting to 50% in 10m unless we see more spikes.
Maya Patel: Appreciate it, Alex. Adds clarity for tonight's coverage.
Alex Kim: Thanks all — will follow up in the morning with short post-mortem if anything noisy slipped through.
